title: Decisions made
heroStatus: Picture frame is In development in Windows 0.1.98, and Family achievements is In development in Android tester33 (build 83), both in release #10. They are off until enabled and still need functional real-device tests. Home dashboard and owner-only Family moments are In development, with partial work only and no usable feature yet. Home intercom, Time capsule and Phone as mouse or touchpad remain Planned.

decisions.answerText: Keep today's pause default and add an easy switch in the player so people choose each time.
decisions.title: Screen-off audio on the phone app
decisions.area: Android phone app: In development, next release
decisions.why: Screen-off still pauses a film by default. The switch in Quality & audio is merged for the next phone release, default off and hidden on TV. It is absent from tester33 (build 83); a functional real-phone retest is still pending.

options.text: Keep it as it is: turning the screen off pauses the video.
The sound keeps playing when the screen turns off.
Keep it as it is, but add an easy switch in the player so people choose each time.
The sound keeps playing only when headphones or Bluetooth are connected.

decisions.answerText: Home dashboard on the picture frame: In development, core preparation only; integration incomplete.
decisions.title: Which new idea to build first
decisions.area: Home dashboard: In development, partial preparation, not usable
decisions.why: I chose the home dashboard first. Core preparation exists, but frame integration, settings and trusted sources are incomplete. There is no usable dashboard yet. The other ideas remain Planned.

options.text: Home intercom and baby monitor: listen or talk between your own devices.
Time capsule: photos and messages sealed until a date you choose.
Home dashboard on the picture frame: what is playing now and reminders.
Phone as a mouse or touchpad for the PC.
None yet. Finish and test what is already built first.

decisions.answerText: Tested on real Linux (Ubuntu in WSL) and an emulated ARM run on Oct 21, 2026; one fault found and fixed (video conversion on a Linux ffmpeg without OpenH264). Not yet tested on a Raspberry Pi, a real NAS, or the Docker image.
decisions.title: How we word the Linux server status
decisions.why: The Linux server remains Beta. Testing on Ubuntu in WSL and an emulated ARM run on Oct 21 found one conversion fault. The libx264 fallback fix for Linux ffmpeg without OpenH264 is merged for the next release; it is not in a newly published Linux package. Raspberry Pi, real NAS and Docker-image checks remain missing.

options.text: Say it plainly: tested on real Linux and in a virtual ARM run, not yet on a Raspberry Pi or a NAS.
Leave the wording as it is.
Change nothing until a real Raspberry Pi or NAS test is done.

decisions.answerText: Skip it for now; the Linux server stays Beta.
decisions.title: Raspberry Pi or NAS test
decisions.why: Real Raspberry Pi, real NAS and Docker-image checks are still missing. I chose to skip those for now and keep the Linux server Beta. The WSL and emulated ARM runs do not replace those checks.

options.text: I buy a Raspberry Pi and run the test when it arrives.
I borrow a NAS or a Raspberry Pi from someone.
Skip it for now and keep the Linux server as Beta.

decisions.answerText: Accept plain HTTP for v1 and say so plainly in the guide.
decisions.title: Picture frame over plain HTTP
decisions.area: Picture frame: In development, in Windows 0.1.98, off until enabled
decisions.why: Windows 0.1.98 includes the picture frame as In development, off until the owner enables it. It is designed to show the owner's chosen photos on a wall tablet or supported browser over home Wi-Fi, using unencrypted plain HTTP. Someone on that same Wi-Fi who has the link can see those chosen photos. Functional device verification is still pending.

options.text: Accept this for the first version, and say it plainly in the guide.
Require an encrypted connection even at home. It is safer, but takes more setup.
Accept it for now, and build the encrypted option next.

decisions.title: Family moments: who sees which photos
decisions.area: Family moments: In development, owner-only, not usable
decisions.why: Only the owner may see the intended Family moments feed. Core access and metadata work exists, but the product UI, owner switch and photo-viewing integration are incomplete. It is not a usable or released feed.

options.text: Use the starting rules: guests see nothing, limited profiles see only folders already allowed for them, and private profiles are never shown.
Let the owner choose, profile by profile, who sees the feed.
Only the owner sees it.

decisions.answerText: The owner profile on that phone is the host.
decisions.title: Family achievements: who is the host
decisions.area: Family achievements: In development, in tester33, off until enabled
decisions.why: Family achievements is In development in tester33. After the host enables it, each person opts in to milestones kept only on that phone. The owner profile on that phone is the host and chooses retention and whether nicknames are allowed; each person must also agree to keep nicknames. There are no badges or leaderboards. Functional real-phone testing is still pending.

options.text: Keep it: the owner profile on that phone is the host.
Any adult profile can be the host.
Use a separate host PIN.

decisions.answerText: Publish the guides only after release #10 is live and the new items have been tested on real devices.
decisions.title: When to publish the how-to guides
decisions.why: Release #10 is live. The new how-to guides remain staged because complete functional real-device retests are still blocked and pending. Version checks and passive diagnostics do not meet the real-device gate.

options.text: After release #10 is live and the new items have been tested on real devices.
Right after the next release is live.
Hold them until I have used each feature myself.

decisions.answerText: Make the notes full width on wide screens too.
decisions.title: Testing status page: how wide the notes are
decisions.why: The notes already sit below each feature row. I chose full-width notes on wide screens too. That update is prepared but is not yet merged into the current website source; its publication has not been verified.

options.text: Leave it as it is.
Show the notes in two columns on wide screens.
Make the notes full width on wide screens too.
